description: Musket and pack - sends the hounds in and shoots whatever they flush out.
_source_note: Rebuilt 5 Nov 2026 from data/reference/coa/witch-hunter.json (37 real CoA Houndmaster talents, role DPS). Replaces a 23-node tree with 1 proc in it and 20 bare numbers. Fourteen of CoA's talents are hound-side and this engine gives a pet three scaling keys and no procs, so those are routed into pet_damage, re-pointed at the Witch Hunter, or dropped - stated per node. Every CoA reference to Rage is translated to Focus.

nodes.name: Expert Shot
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Shadowblast by up to 20% and your chance to hit by up to 4%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim, and already a scalar in CoA over 2 ranks, so it stays one. Authored as the full-investment CEILING at one rank and left to the rank policy to spread - writing CoA's rank-1 value with ranks=2 and then having the policy bump it to 3 is what left three descriptions in this tree quoting a per-rank number that no longer existed.

nodes.name: Dark Mind
nodes.description: Increases your critical strike chance by 25% of your Intellect.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Level 30 Passive. Increases your critical strike rating by 25% of your Intellect.' A live conversion: crit_chance is in STAT_CONVERSION_TARGETS (mapping to crit_chance_physical) and intellect is a source. Pairs with Boltslinger's Arbalist as the second reason a physical Witch Hunter wants Intellect.

nodes.name: Houndfeeder
nodes.description: Increases your critical strike chance by 4% and your hounds' damage by 4%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the critical strike chance of you and your Shadow Hound by 4%.' A pet's crit is not one of the three keys entities/pet.py reads off its owner, so the hound half becomes pet_damage - the closest thing to 'your hound hits harder' that the engine will actually apply. crit_chance_physical is a PERCENT and pet_damage is a FRACTION, in the same effects block.

nodes.name: Trapper
nodes.description: Reduces the cooldown of your Trap spells by 25%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Reduces the cooldown of your Trap spells by -25%.' Written out per ability because there is no key for a named group of abilities. POSITIVE is the reduction direction, which is the opposite of CoA's own '-25%' notation.

nodes.name: Hail of Gunfire
nodes.description: Increases your haste by 10%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases your ranged haste by 10%.' No separate ranged haste pool exists, and haste here means acting more often on the turn meter.

nodes.name: Sharpshooter
nodes.description: Shadowblast returns 15 Focus.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Level 20 Passive. Casting Shadowblast now regenerates 5% of your maximum mana.' The class has no mana - Witch Hunter is Focus-only - so this becomes Focus, as a flat amount rather than a percentage of the pool. Shadowblast is the filler, so this is what pays for the spec's expensive casts.

nodes.name: Dark Ranger
nodes.description: Increases your hounds' damage by up to 10%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases the Shadow damage dealt by your Shadow Hounds by 5%.' pet_damage is school-agnostic - it scales the pet's attack_power and spell_power together - so the Shadow restriction is lost. A FRACTION, not points.

nodes.name: Expulsion of Evil
nodes.description: Your ranged attacks have a 5% chance to make Houndmaster's Call ready again at once.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Direct ranged attacks and abilities now have a 5% chance to reset the cooldown of Houndmaster's Call.' Ports directly - CoA's 5% kept, with a 1-turn internal cooldown so it cannot chain off one flurry.

nodes.name: Reload
nodes.description: Reduces the cooldown of Quickdraw by 35%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Reduces the cooldown of Quickdraw by 4 sec.' Quickdraw's CoA cooldown is 10 sec, so 4 sec is 40% of it; expressed as a percentage because cooldowns are counted in turns here and a flat 4 would round to one turn either way. Trimmed to 35% rather than 40% because Expulsion of Evil and Scent of Magic are already shortening this spec's cooldowns.

nodes.name: Pure Agony
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike damage of Quickdraw by 50%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim. ability_*_crit_damage is in the dynamic key family the engine resolves by name, and it is a FRACTION - unlike ability_*_crit beside it, which is a percent.

nodes.name: Coordinated Killing
nodes.description: Unleashing the hounds whips you up too, increasing your damage by 10% for 3 turns.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Casting Unleash the Hounds now casts Shadow Rage on you for 10 sec.' THIS is the buildable Shadow Rage, and it absorbs CoA's other two. CoA's base Shadow Rage talent puts the buff on the HOUND off a Shadowblast cast, which no key reaches, and Lethal Pursuit adds 3 more stacks to it - so the stack count here is 4, which is CoA's 1 plus Lethal Pursuit's 3, rather than shipping Lethal Pursuit as a separate node that edits this one's payload (no key does that either). on_cast, not on_damage_cast: Unleash the Hounds is a summon and deals no damage, so a damage trigger would never fire.

nodes.name: Kennel Master
nodes.description: Increases your hounds' damage and health by up to 12%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Casting Unleash The Hounds now has a 25% chance to summon an additional Lesser Shadow Hound for 15 sec.' A proc COULD cast_ability the summon again, but that is a summon re-triggering its own trigger - the Rockslide self-chain pattern is fine for a damage spell and genuinely dangerous for a pet summon, since nothing caps how many hounds exist. Routed into the hounds you already have instead, which is the honest version of 'more hound'.

nodes.name: Darkrider
nodes.description: Reduces the Focus cost of Shadowblast, Vault and Unleash the Hounds by 15%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Reduces the Rage cost of Shadowblast, Vault, and Unleash the Hounds by -10.' Rage -> Focus, and the flat 10 becomes a percentage so it does not go stale against three different costs. POSITIVE reduces.

nodes.name: Scent of Magic
nodes.description: Your critical strikes bring Houndmaster's Call a turn closer to ready.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Critical strikes now apply Scent of Magic for 15 sec, causing your Shadow Hound's next Shadow Leap to incur a 10 sec reduced cooldown.' Shadow Leap is the hound's own ability and has no cooldown a talent can reach, so this is pointed at Houndmaster's Call - the player-side ability that sends the hounds in, which is what CoA's version is really shortening. turns:1 knocks one turn off rather than resetting outright.

nodes.name: Darkhunter
nodes.description: Quickdraw leaves your next hits 20% stronger for 2 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Quickdraw now additionally causes your next Darkslayer within 15 seconds to be instant cast.' There are no cast times here, so making something instant is worth nothing and there is nothing to set. Repriced as damage on the window CoA describes, which keeps the Quickdraw-into-Darkslayer sequence worth doing. Also carries CoA's Low Dawn, which compresses a channel that likewise does not exist.

nodes.name: Decimate
nodes.description: Increases your hounds' damage by 15% and your armor penetration by 10%.
nodes._source: CoA: '2 min cooldown. Empowers your Shadow Hounds for 20 sec, granting them 30% increased damage and haste and allowing them to ignore Armor.' Built as a passive rather than an activated window, because a 2-minute cooldown is not a shape this tree has and 30% for 20 seconds every two minutes averages out near 15% always. Pet haste is not a reachable key. 'Ignore Armor' is the Witch Hunter's own armor penetration, since there is no pet penetration key.

nodes.name: Silver Bullets
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Darkslayer by up to 30%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the damage of Darkslayer by 10%, increased by an additional 10% against Undead.' No effect key reads the target's creature type, so the Undead bonus is dropped and CoA's base 10% kept.

nodes.name: Rampaging Hounds
nodes.description: Increases your hounds' damage and health by 10%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Shadow Hounds melee attacks now cleave 1 additional nearby enemy.' No key adds a target to anything, least of all to a pet's auto attack, which no talent touches at all. Routed into the two pet keys that do work. This node and Kennel Master are both 'CoA wanted more hound and the engine offers pet_damage', which is why they sit in different tiers rather than next to each other reading as the same pick twice.

nodes.name: Anguish
nodes.description: Your shadow damage has a 10% chance to make Darkflock ready again at once.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Shadow damage dealt now has a 5% chance to reduce the channel time of your next Darkflock within 15 seconds by -50%.' Channels do not exist, so there is no channel time to halve. Rebuilt as getting Darkflock back sooner, which is what halving its channel bought in CoA, and raised 5% -> 10% because a cooldown reset is worth less than halving a cast.

nodes.name: Bringer of Darkness
nodes.description: Repulse resets the cooldown of Vault and returns 10 Focus.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Repulse now resets the cooldown of Vault and makes your next Vault within 6 sec free of cost.' The reset ports exactly. 'Free of cost' needs an ability cost key reachable from a status effect, and cost keys are read only through get_talent_effects() which never includes status effects - so it becomes a Focus refund of its own, which is the same saving by a route that fires.

nodes.name: Defender of Darkshire
nodes.description: Your critical strikes quicken you, increasing your haste by 10% for 2 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Critical strikes with ranged auto attacks now increase the melee haste of your Shadow Hounds by 10% for 5 sec.' Pet haste is not a reachable key, so the buff lands on the Witch Hunter instead - CoA's number and the same trigger, pointed at the one of the two of you a talent can touch. 2-turn internal cooldown so a crit streak does not keep it permanently up.

nodes.name: Veiled in Darkness
nodes.description: Increases your attack power by 5%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'A veil of dark magic encircles you at all times, granting 5% increased Attack Power to party and raid members within 100 yds.' A talent effect applies to its own character and there is no aura mechanism, so the description says 'your' rather than promising the party a buff it will never receive. attack_power_pct takes percentage POINTS.

nodes.name: Loksey's Journal
nodes.description: Increases the damage your damage-over-time effects deal by 10%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the damage of Shadow Rage by 20% of your ranged attack power.' Shadow Rage in this tree is a damage_dealt_pct buff, not an ability with damage of its own, so there is nothing for that to scale - and no key adds attack power scaling to a status effect. Rebuilt as DoT damage, which this spec has real use for: Darkflock and Death Trap are both periodic.

nodes.name: Rearmament
nodes.description: Reduces the cooldown of your Traps by a further 20%.
nodes._source: CoA: '5 min cooldown. Arm yourself against evil, resetting the cooldown of all Traps and Decimate.' Frontier has no witch_hunter_rearmament ability to unlock, and a 5-minute reset button is not a shape this tree has, so it becomes a permanent cut to the same cooldowns it would have reset. Stacks with Trapper at tier 0, deliberately: both are 'traps come back faster' and together they are the trap build.

nodes.name: Daredevil
nodes.description: When you are badly hurt, Vault becomes ready again at once and your hounds surge, dealing 20% more damage for 3 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Level 40 Passive. When you take damage that would reduce your health to 35% or less, you summon 3 lesser Shadow Hounds and reset the cooldown of Vault. Can only occur once every 2 min.' The Vault reset ports exactly. The health GATE does not: no proc payload reads the carrier's own health threshold, so it is a 15% chance on taking damage with a 5-turn internal cooldown, which is roughly CoA's once-every-2-minutes. The three summoned hounds are not buildable from a proc (see Kennel Master), so the surge lands as damage instead and the description says 'your hounds surge' without promising new ones.

nodes.name: Deal With The Devil
nodes.description: Increases your shadow critical strike damage by 50%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your and your Shadow Hounds critical damage dealt with Shadow damage is increased by 50%, but the cost of your spells and abilities is increased by 25%.' <school>_crit_damage_pct is a key the engine builds by interpolation, so shadow_crit_damage_pct is live. The hound half is unreachable. THE DRAWBACK IS DROPPED, and that is a real loss of CoA's design: cost keys are reduction-signed, so a 25% surcharge has to be written negative, which is indistinguishable from the sign error the audit now flags and which eight talents in this project already made. Flagged rather than faked - this node is strictly better than CoA's.

nodes.name: Lethal Pursuit
nodes.description: Increases your hounds' damage by 15%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Shadow Rage now also grants your Shadow Hounds 10% increased haste and it now stacks 3 additional times.' Pet haste is unreachable, and the extra stacks are already folded into Coordinated Killing's payload at tier 2 (4 stacks = CoA's 1 plus these 3), because no key edits a sibling node's effect. What is left is the intent - the hounds get more out of a long fight - as pet damage.

nodes.name: Feast of Talons
nodes.description: Darkflock sends the crows out wide, splashing 40% of its damage onto up to 5 enemies and leaving them bleeding shadow for 3 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Striking at least 5 enemies with Darkflock now causes you to unleash a flock of crows around each enemy struck, dealing Twilight Damage over 9 sec.' The 5-enemy THRESHOLD is not buildable - no payload counts how many targets the triggering cast hit - so the capstone fires on every Darkflock and spreads to 5, which is the same shape pointed the other way round. 9 sec is 3 turns. Twilight is not a damage school here (the six are arcane, fire, frost, nature, shadow, holy), so both halves are shadow - CoA's Twilight is shadow-and-holy blended, and shadow is the half this spec is built on.
